checkin_hall.verdict: Not at the fern bar yet. The wide is the best frame and comes close to the film's look. The haze shaft over the only lit desk, the dark closed row and the chrome posts leading in all read as the night check-in hall. The other three frames each have a fault that would look amateur on YouTube. SHOULDER is the weakest. It sits about one stop hotter than the rest of the stage (raw mean 75 against 35-49 for the other cameras). Because of that, Dawn's dark umber elegantsuit reads as a light grey open-collar shirt, which breaks continuity with the wide and the profile, where it reads dark. It also turns the dark counter top and the dark passport into flat light-grey slabs. Her face is hot on the forehead, has empty black eye sockets from top light, carries a teal-green cast on the jaw and neck in the raw, and shows a black seam line at the hairline. Her eyeline goes level rather than up to him. Her hand is splayed and stiff, the fingers are spread and straight, and a black band at the wrist reads as a bracelet. The bottom 20% of the frame is a featureless grey counter slab, which the brief bans by name. PROFILE stages well and the bags read dark. But the monitor face is turned to the camera and Dawn more than to the agent, so he seems to read the edge of a screen that faces her. His face gets no visible screen spill: it is the same value as his suit and has no cool lift. Dawn's lower legs read as bare stone with dark socks and chunky trainer-like shoes. The scale display post makes a dark vertical bar at the frame edge, and the foreground plinth is a dark slab cut by the bottom edge. SCALE hits its brief: the duffel is in focus, the display is the brightest thing in frame and Dawn is out of shot. But the right third is empty black floor, and the display face is a flat grey card that throws no light onto the post or the bags. The 'conveyor' behind is an empty trough with rails that reads as a cage, not as rubber belting. WIDE: the queue belts are thin taut rods, not about 5 cm webbing with a sag, and the front-left post stands unconnected. The trolley reads as a supermarket wire cart. The closed desks are identical grey boxes with no workstation detail. The right wall is a large featureless dark slab. A big glowing blank sign panel at top centre-right competes with Dawn's island. Across the stage the grade crushes 25-29% of pixels to 8/255 or below in the wide and scale frames. Materials are generic: the counter is a plain grey box with no laminate, edge banding or kick plate, and the ledge reads light instead of the brief's dark top. Compared with the craft in the reference films (koi-pond-keycap's dense, worn, bevelled materials), surface detail is thin everywhere except the bags and the stanchions.

fixes.problem: Frame is about one stop hotter than the other cameras: Dawn's dark umber suit reads as a light grey shirt (a continuity break and the 'bare skin' risk people.py warns about), the forehead is near clipping, and the dark passport and counter top read light grey.
fixes.fix: Bring the shoulder key down by about 1 EV: either set a per-camera exposure 0.8-1.0 lower than now, or cut the downlight/area light that keys Dawn by 50% and lower it so it grazes less. Check the raw: the jacket should average under about 55/255 and the forehead peak under about 215/255. Do not grey the suit tint.

fixes.problem: Dawn's face: black eye sockets from pure top light, a teal-green cast on the jaw and neck (raw), a dark seam line between the sculpted hair cap and the forehead, and an eyeline that is level rather than up to the agent.
fixes.fix: Add a weak, soft, cool fill from the agent's side at counter height: an area light about 0.4x0.25 m, 1.2 m in front of her face at z about 1.15, aimed at her eyes, 2-4 W, colour (0.75,0.82,1.0), so the sockets lift to readable mid-dark. Find and remove the green spill source (probably a coloured screen or emission near her chin): set its colour to neutral-cool (0.62,0.72,1.0) or drop its power. Close the hair seam: offset the hair mesh 1-2 mm outward, or shrinkwrap its lower edge onto the scalp. Pose with head down about -10 deg (chin up) and turn about 5-8 deg toward the agent's eye position, and raise the agent's eye height 5-8 cm (a platform behind the counter), so she visibly looks up.

fixes.problem: Her hand on the ledge is splayed: the fingers are straight and spread wide, the thumb sticks out, and a black band at the wrist (sleeve cuff or lining) reads as a bracelet.
fixes.fix: In rigged.pose_figure, curl every finger 15-20 deg at each joint, close the finger spread to 3-5 deg, and bring the thumb in along the index finger. Pull the sleeve end back 1-2 cm, or set the cuff inner face to the suit material so there is no dark band. Keep the wrist about 20 cm out from the body centre, as the brief says. Re-check the hand from the profile camera too.

fixes.problem: The agent's monitor reads as turned toward Dawn and the camera, not toward him, and his face is not lit by it: it has the same value as his suit and no cool lift. The story beat (he reads the weight on his screen) does not land.
fixes.fix: Raise MON's yaw from 48 to about 68-72 deg so the screen normal points at his eyes, accepting a more oblique view of the face from the profile camera. Add an area light the size of the screen (0.37x0.2 m) 2 cm in front of mon_screen, facing the same way, 4-8 W, colour (0.6,0.75,1.0), with spread about 60 deg. His cheek, nose and brow should come out clearly brighter and cooler than his suit in the graded frame. Keep his head down 15-20 deg.

fixes.problem: The counter fills the bottom 20% of the frame as a flat light-grey slab with a white edge line. The passport is a light grey tile and does not read as a passport.
fixes.fix: Make the counter top the brief's dark solid surface: base about 0.035-0.05, roughness 0.45-0.55, with a faint roughness-variation noise (scale about 40) and 3-5 fine scuffs. Tilt the camera up or raise aim z by about 3 cm so the counter fills 12% of the frame or less. Passport: keep the cover value about 0.05, raise roughness to 0.7, round the corners to 4 mm, add a slightly lighter page-block strip 1.5 mm inset on three edges, and turn it about 12 deg off-square to the counter edge.

fixes.problem: The queue belts are thin straight rods, not webbing, and the front-left post stands alone. The trolley reads as a supermarket wire cart.
fixes.fix: Build each belt as a 50 mm x 2 mm black webbing strip (roughness 0.6, faint weave bump) between post heads, with 1-2 cm of sag at mid-span (a 3-segment curve). Run a belt from the front-left post into the lane, or delete that post. Replace or rebuild the trolley as a flat-deck airport baggage trolley: a low deck, a tall push-frame handle with a brake bar and two large rear wheels, no wire basket. Put one stray piece of luggage or nothing on it.

fixes.problem: Set dressing is thin and cloned: the closed desks are identical bare boxes, the right wall is a large featureless dark slab, and a large glowing blank sign panel at top centre-right competes with Dawn's lit island.
fixes.fix: Vary the closed desks: put a dark monitor (screen_off, slight reflection) on each, a retractable belt hooked across two of them, and one chair pushed back. At Dawn's desk add a bag-tag printer (0.2x0.25x0.15 m) and a boarding-pass printer beside the monitor. Break the right wall: add a structural column 0.6 m wide at about two-thirds of the way along, or a closed service door with a 2 cm warm light leak at the floor. Cut the big overhead sign panel's emission by about 60%, or make it an unlit dark panel, so the brightest area in the frame is the counter island.

fixes.problem: The right third is empty black floor. The display is a flat grey card that lights nothing. The conveyor behind reads as an empty railed cage.
fixes.fix: Move the display post onto the counter side of the scale, 10-15 cm from the plinth edge, with its face toward the passenger, then reframe about 0.25 m to the right (or go from 50 to about 40 mm) so the display sits on the upper-right third above the duffel. Add an area light 0.12x0.07 m at the display face, 0.5-1 W, cool, so its post top and the near edge of the duffel catch a little light. Build a real conveyor: dark ribbed rubber belt (bump stripes every 6 mm across the belt, base 0.02, roughness 0.75), a steel side skirt and a black rubber flap curtain at the back opening.

fixes.problem: The grade crushes 25-29% of pixels to 8/255 or below in the wide and scale frames. The ceiling, the far end of the row and the right wall go to pure black.
fixes.fix: In the grade, lift the toe by about +4 to +6 on the 0-255 scale, or lower the black point. Alternatively add a very dim cool area light (0.5-1 W/m2) along the far end of the closed row so the dark desks and the left glazing keep detail at about 10-25/255 after grading.

fixes.problem: Dawn's lower legs read as bare stone with dark socks and chunky, trainer-like soles, which looks wrong with a skirt suit. The display post makes a dark vertical bar near the right edge, and the plinth is a dark slab cut by the bottom of the frame.
fixes.fix: Check shoes04 in the raw. If its sole is thick, use the plainest flat shoe from shoes01-06 and tint it BLACK_SHOE with roughness 0.5. Give the legs dark sheer tights by tinting the lower-leg skin to about 0.15, or lengthen the skirt, so no light/dark band appears at the ankle. Move the camera about 0.2 m toward -Y, or slide the display post 0.3 m, so the post leaves the frame edge or reads clearly as the display. Tilt the camera up about 2 deg so the plinth's front edge sits inside the frame, not tangent to the bottom edge.

fixes.problem: The counter reads as a plain grey box with no laminate, edge banding or kick plate. It lacks the wear and bevel detail of the reference films.
fixes.fix: Counter front: a fine laminate (low-contrast wood-grain or speckle noise at scale about 80, base about 0.12, roughness 0.4), a 2 mm edge band of slightly darker value on every panel edge, and a brushed steel kick plate 0.10 m tall at the base with a 3 mm bevel. Add a few darker scuff marks low on the passenger side and a slightly worn, rubbed-shiny edge on the ledge where passengers lean.

inspection_room.verdict: Round 3 is close, but it is not at a professional level yet. The best frames are empty and wide. Empty is a real Ch 11 image: a lit island on the steel, the light under the door, the whole scanner and conveyor in frame, and the bags at the right values. Wide is good establishing grammar. The cast still gives it away as amateur. In two_shot, Dawn's jacket and blouse render at the same value as her stone skin (raw crop), so from the front she reads as a nude mannequin with a modelled bust. That is the single worst problem in the set. The officers' caps read as pale stone pancakes. From overhead they are flat white discs like plates. In two_shot, Officer A's cap sits on the back of his crown. Overhead, Officer A's hand is a bright white mitt on the tote, 24% of the graded frame is crushed to pure black, and the 'open' extra bag reads closed, so the discovery beat is carried only by the handbags. The tag close-up has the right idea, but the card puckers radially round the eyelet like stretched cloth. It has dark gouge or mesh-tear marks at lower left, the grade turns it to near-white grey instead of manila, and the twine is a smooth tube. The charcoal case reads mid-grey here but black in the wide. The scanner is a plain grey box. Its monitor is a white card with no bezel and no spill, its curtain is flat panels, and in the wide its right half sinks into black. In two_shot the ceiling takes the top ~45% of the frame, and Officer A's open hand overlaps the bottom of the bright vision panel (a tangency). The officers' shoes are statue-grey, not black (wide, under the bench). Noise, fireflies and aliasing are clean. The tote grades to khaki or mustard, not cognac.

fixes.problem: Dawn's suit reads as bare stone skin from the front: in the raw two_shot the jacket and blouse are the same value as her face, with a modelled bust and no garment edge, so she reads as undressed. The tint in cloth() is evidently not landing on female_elegantsuit01, because the MIX lookup misses it or the garment's base colour is fed elsewhere.
fixes.fix: In inspection_room.dawn(), after cloth(), force the colour. For every material slot on Dawn_female_elegantsuit01, unlink Principled 'Base Color' and set it to (0.085, 0.08, 0.075). Keep roughness at 0.92 and Specular IOR Level at 0.04. Darken the blouse_v rgb to (0.16, 0.155, 0.145). Then print each slot's resolved base colour, and check in a 960x540 two_shot test that the jacket's mean value is no more than 45% of her face's. Add real lapel edges (hem_thickness 0.008 on the front opening) and two 12 mm dark buttons, so the front reads as a jacket.

fixes.problem: The officers' caps read as pale stone. Seen from straight down they are flat light discs like dinner plates. In two_shot Officer A's cap sits back on the crown like a pancake, and Officer B's cap merges with the dark ceiling.
fixes.fix: Give the peaked-cap material navy cloth: crown base (0.025, 0.032, 0.06), roughness 0.75, Specular IOR Level 0.1. Make the peak a separate material, black (0.01, 0.01, 0.012), roughness 0.3. Seat the cap: rotate it forward about 12-15 deg on its local X, lower it 1.5-2 cm and move it 1 cm forward, so the peak shades the brow and the band touches the forehead above the ears. From overhead the crown should then read as a dark navy oval with a visible black peak.

fixes.problem: The discovery beat is weak. The 'open' extra bag reads closed, Officer A's right hand is a glowing white mitt (the brightest thing on the bench), and 24% of the graded frame sits at 0-3/255, so the floor round the bench, Dawn's legs and the operator crush.
fixes.fix: Swap in extra-bag-open with its zip mouth turned to the lens and the zip parted 8-10 cm (scale the opening's verts, or a lattice on the top panel). Put a slightly lighter lining (0.10 grey) visible inside, so the opening reads as a dark slot with a lit lip. For the hands from overhead, call hands_stone(value=0.22) for this beat, or light-link the troffer's area light to exclude a 'hands' collection and give them a 0.5x copy. Lift the overhead floor: cut the grade's vignette strength for this camera by about 40%, or add a 6-10 W area light, 2 m square, linked to the floor only, so the tile 1.5 m from the bench sits at roughly 6-10% value, not 0.

fixes.problem: The tag looks like crumpled fabric, not card stock. It has radial puckers round the eyelet, a soft melted lower edge, and dark gouge/tear artefacts at lower left (raw, around x 630-720, y 510-560). The raw cream colour grades to near-white grey, and it is the brightest thing in the frame. The twine is a smooth white tube. The charcoal case reads mid-grey, which breaks continuity with the wide, where it is black.
fixes.fix: Remove the eyelet pucker and displacement and rebuild the tag as a flat 0.35 mm solidified card. Give it one soft bend (Simple Deform BEND 10-15 deg about its short axis, two-thirds of the way down), one dog-eared corner and a fine paper-fibre bump (noise scale 2000, strength 0.05). Delete whatever produces the gouges: check for flipped normals or a displace texture hole. Manila albedo (0.50, 0.40, 0.26), roughness 0.9, so after the cool grade it stays buff, not white. Make the twine a 0.9 mm two-ply twist (curve bevel with an offset profile, or a wave-texture bump along the length) in warm jute (0.42, 0.34, 0.22), with sparse 0.3-1 mm fibre hairs. Drop the camera exposure from -3.5 to about -4.1, or dim the raking light about 35%, so the case reads charcoal.

fixes.problem: The X-ray scanner is an undetailed grey box. The monitor is a white card with no bezel and no light spill, the tunnel curtain is flat vertical panels, and in the wide the right half and side vanish into black. Three unexplained pale boxes on the right wall pull the eye.
fixes.fix: Bevel the housing's edges at 2 cm. Add side access-panel seams (2 mm grooves) and a kick plate. Replace the curtain with 9-10 separate 4 mm lead-rubber strips (0.02 grey, roughness 0.6) with 3 mm gaps and slight random X rotation (+/-3 deg). Make the monitor a 3 cm dark bezel (0.03) around a recessed face emitting cool grey at strength 0.8-1.2, on a short arm, with an 8-12 W area light 15 cm in front aimed at the scanner top. Add a small operator console (a slanted keyboard plinth) on the near side. Add a weak 10-15 W area light or a green status lamp at the exit end, so the scanner's silhouette and right side hold at about 8-12% value. Darken the three right-wall boxes to the wall's value, or remove them.

fixes.problem: Framing: the ceiling grid fills about 45% of the frame, so the people sit low and Dawn is cut at the thighs. Officer A's open palm overlaps the bottom of the bright vision panel (a tangency), and the operator's behind-back hand pokes out splayed and white at frame right.
fixes.fix: Lower the aim from z 1.82 to about 1.62 (or lift the camera to z 1.35), keeping the whole troffer in frame, so the ceiling takes at most about 30%. Move the duffel_hover target 8-10 cm toward the bench and 5 cm down, or slide the camera 10 cm in Y, so the palm sits in clear wall below the panel with at least 3 cm of separation. For OfficerB in ch00 set fingers 55 and tuck the 'behind' wrists 5 cm closer to the spine, so no hand breaks his silhouette.

fixes.problem: Officer A's 'palm-up' gesture reads palm-down and splayed, as if he is pressing on the duffel. The operator's shoes visible under the bench are statue-grey, not black.
fixes.fix: Supinate the forearm a further 40-60 deg so the palm faces up, with fingers curled 20-25 deg and the thumb slightly out. Raise the hand to about 8 cm above the duffel's top surface and keep the elbow bent 25-35 deg away from the body. Set both officers' shoe material to black leather (0.015, 0.015, 0.017), roughness 0.35.

fixes.problem: The cognac tote grades to pale khaki or mustard, not cognac leather. In overhead it reads yellow beside a near-white hand.
fixes.fix: Shift the tote's hue about -0.02 back toward red-brown and lower val about 15% (more saturation, +0.1). Check that the graded frame shows a mid-dark tan-brown (graded sRGB roughly 120/85/55), not beige. Add a slightly darker edge-paint line on the handles and seams (an AO-driven 0.7x darken).

fixes.problem: Seen straight down, the bench top shows horizontal light streaks round the tote that read as wood grain on steel.
fixes.fix: Cut the brushed-steel streak contrast on the bench top by about half (lower the wave/noise texture's ColorRamp spread or the anisotropy to about 0.3), and add a faint large-scale smudge/wipe roughness variation instead.

departure_gate.verdict:
This is not at fern level yet (mean about 5.3). Seated is the strongest frame: the pose is readable, the suitcase reads charcoal, the perforated steel seats are believable and nothing clips. Window has the best idea, Dawn's back against the floodlit nose, and is close to working. Wide fails its brief. There is no single downlight pool. The floor is lit evenly to mid grey from the foreground rows to the glass, so the eye goes straight to the glossy airliner and the bright podium screen, not to Dawn. She is tiny, and an untextured grey post stands right in front of her and her suitcase. Problems that run through all three frames:
- From behind, Dawn's sculpted bun reads as a backwards baseball cap (wide and window).
- Her shoes are slipper-like clogs with an embossed brand-like stamp on each toe, which breaks the no-logos rule. With bare stone legs and dark ankle socks, the wardrobe reads odd.
- The carpet tiles are a large, smooth vinyl checkerboard with no fibre.
- The airliner is toy-like: oversized bubble cockpit windows, a short run of about 10 cabin windows, a plastic gloss, and no clear jet bridge-to-door connection.
- The window glass carries scattered white dashes (reflected linear lights) that float in the sky like artefacts.
- Seated does not deliver the f/1.8 the brief asks for: the background rows are nearly sharp, and the bottom third is an empty grey floor slab.
- Graded frames crush 17-19% of pixels to black in wide and window, mostly on the window frame and the wall that should carry the place.
Technically the frames are clean: no fireflies, mild grain, some denoiser smear on the aircraft.

fixes.problem: No lit island. The whole floor is evenly mid grey, Dawn is not the brightest thing near her, and the plane and podium screen pull the eye.
fixes.fix: Bring the general ceiling and area lights over the seating to 10-15% of their current power, or switch off the rows nearer the camera. Light Dawn with one spot downlight about 3.2 m above her seat (point at her lap, spot_size about 40 deg, blend 0.35, radius 0.05, about 400-800 W, slightly warm 4000 K). Aim for a visible circle of about 1.5 m on the carpet, with the area around her at least 1.5 stops brighter than the empty rows. Keep 2-3 weak downlights deeper in the room at about 15% so the rows stay readable, not black. Cut the apron floodlight on the aircraft by about 1 stop so the glass is no longer the brightest area.

fixes.problem: An untextured grey rectangular post (about image x 490-530, y 400-580) stands in front of Dawn and her suitcase and blocks the subject. A second plain slab post stands at right (about x 1150-1175).
fixes.fix: Delete the post or move it at least 2 m away, out of the line between the camera and Dawn. If it is meant as a charging pillar, bevel it (0.01 m), give it a dark brushed-metal material and set it against a column, not in the aisle. Do the same for the right-hand slab or remove it.

fixes.problem: Each shoe toe carries an embossed brand-like stamp, which breaks the no-logos rule. The clog and dark ankle-sock look, with bare grey stone legs, reads odd.
fixes.fix: In people.dawn() usage (pose and place only, so do it in the stage module after the build), find the shoe object's material and disconnect or zero its normal/bump map (Normal Map strength 0). Or report the problem to the orchestrator so dawn() switches to plain shoes01/shoes02. If the wardrobe allows, give the legs a dark tights tint (value about 0.08) so legs and socks read as one garment.

fixes.problem: From behind and at 3/4 back, Dawn's bun reads as a backwards cap with a brim (also in wide).
fixes.fix: Move the bun lower, to the nape (about 4-5 cm down), and scale it to about 0.7, or flatten it so no brim-like edge sticks out. Check it from the window and wide cameras. If the bun mesh is fixed in people.py, flag it for the orchestrator.

fixes.problem: The airliner looks like a toy: bubble cockpit windows that are too large, about 10 cabin windows bunched at the front, a plastic sheen, no nose gear, and the jet bridge does not clearly reach the L1 door.
fixes.fix: Base colour value about 0.35, roughness 0.45, coat 0. Make the cockpit glazing 4-6 flat slanted panes of about 0.55x0.45 m, set into the nose curve. Run cabin windows along the full fuselage at 0.53 m pitch (0.25x0.35 m, dim warm emission 0.3). Add the nose gear (strut plus two wheels on the ground, with a contact shadow). Extend the jet bridge cab to meet the fuselage just behind the cockpit on the port side, with a bellows box. Add 2-3 apron items: a tug, a belt loader at the forward hold and 3-4 cones.

fixes.problem: The carpet tiles read as a smooth vinyl checkerboard. Large tiles alternate tone, with no fibre and no seams.
fixes.fix: Use 0.5 m tiles with alternating quarter-turn grain. Keep value variation between tiles to about ±3%. Make seams 2 mm and slightly darker. Add fibre with a Noise texture (scale about 600-900) into Bump at strength 0.12, plus a directional wave texture for pile direction. Roughness 0.95, specular about 0.2. Base value low (about 0.12-0.15) so the floor sits under Dawn, not at her value.

fixes.problem: The f/1.8 isn't there: the second and third rows are nearly sharp. The bottom third is an empty grey floor slab.
fixes.fix: Set the camera to 75-85 mm, DOF on, fstop 1.8, focus_object an empty at Dawn's chest. Lower the camera to about 1.05 m and push in, so the frame bottom lands about 25 cm below her shoes while keeping the feet whole. Let her downlight make a falloff pool on the floor around her feet and the suitcase so the floor is not flat.

fixes.problem: White dashes scattered in the sky and across the upper glass read as artefacts, not reflections.
fixes.fix: Either build a real ceiling grid with linear fixtures, so the reflections line up as a coherent perspective of the interior, or lower the glass's reflectivity (IOR about 1.15, or mix the glass with Transparent at about 0.85) and remove or hide the floating linear emitters the glass catches. Keep a faint reflection of Dawn's downlight and seat row in the glass for realism.

fixes.problem: The vertical mullion and the jet bridge edge near image x 770 run tangent to Dawn's head. The plane nose is the brightest value, right beside her, and her head merges with it.
fixes.fix: Move the camera about 0.25 m left (or Dawn one seat right) so her head sits clear inside one glass pane, against the darker jet bridge. Add a narrow rim light (area light 0.3x0.3 m, about 30 W, above and behind her) so her shoulders and head edge separate. Drop the nose floodlight by about 0.7 stop.

fixes.problem: The podium screen is a flat white patch with no spill or bezel contrast, and the podium reads as a thin table frame. The far wall and ceiling crush to black, so the room loses its shape.
fixes.fix: Set the screen emission to about 1.5 with a cool tint. Add a 15-20 mm bezel at value 0.04, plus a weak area light (0.4x0.3 m, about 5 W) in front of the screen so it spills onto the desk top and the agent side. Close the podium front with a beveled panel (value 0.2, roughness 0.6). Add a dark ceiling plane at about 3.4 m with 4-6 recessed downlight cans (rim emission only). Give the back wall low grazing light (a wall-washer area light, about 20 W) so it holds at about 8-12% grey after the grade instead of 0.

fixes.problem: A small white ladder-stripe patch on the suitcase side reads as a logo or label.
fixes.fix: Find the material slot or UV region of that patch on dawn-suitcase and darken it to match the shell (about value 0.06), or turn the case about 15 deg so the patch faces away from the camera.

detention_corridor.verdict: Clearly better than round 2. The corridor now opens out of walls you can read, with a real pool / dead gap / pool rhythm, the door panel no longer reads as a porthole, and the chair frame is a lit island at fern's level. It is still not pro level. Shot edge-on from 17 cm, the envelope insert no longer reads as a sealed envelope. The cell-door close-up still shows streaky, wood-grain paint, the prop's melted hinge and hatch, and a black-and-white muddle behind the bars. In the corridor, the floor pools (about 180/255 graded) still outshine the amber doorway (about 122) that should be the frame's destination.

fixes.problem: The round-2 fix overshot. From 17 cm above the top on a 70 mm lens the envelope is seen almost edge-on: a white sliver about 380 x 60 px with a 20 mm curl rising to a sharp point. It reads as a folded strip of paper or a paper boat. The flap V, the seal and the envelope's proportions, which are the whole beat ('a sealed envelope'), are gone. The previous top-down version read better as an envelope.
fixes.fix: In CAMERAS['envelope'], raise the camera to about 18-22 deg above the table: loc about (0.45, 14.5, 1.15), aim about (-0.08, 15.95, 0.72), lens 70-75, fstop 2.8, focus on fx_envelope. Adjust the aim at preview so that the envelope sits on the lower-third line with the top flap's V and its tip clearly visible, the top of the empty chair's back sits about 10% below the frame top, and the table stays under about 45% of the frame. In envelope(), reduce the curl from h += 0.020 * max(0, 1 - q/cq)**2 to about 0.008, with cq widened from 0.065 to 0.09, so the corner lifts gently instead of rising to a peak. Keep the pendant_pool MOVES offset so the curl and the body still throw their shadow toward the lens.

fixes.problem: Door paint: thin vertical dark streaks run over the whole leaf around and below the window and over the frame. In the close-up they read as wood grain or rain streaks on steel, which the brief warns against. The 3 mm panel dents that should show under the raking key do not read, so the leaf is a flat blue-grey field with streaks.
fixes.fix: In detention_corridor_mats.door_steel(): restrict the 'win' zone to under the frame's bottom edge (band pz 0.95-1.18 instead of 0.95-1.82) so the field round the window stays clean. Tighten runs from maprange(0.6, 0.66) to (0.72, 0.75) and drips from (0.9, 0.97) to (0.96, 0.985), and drop the streak mix factor from 0.7 to 0.3, leaving a few drips under the frame and above the hatch. Raise the dent bump distance from 0.003 to 0.006 at noise scale 1.6, so door_rake shows soft panel undulation. Add a broad roughness variation of 0.45-0.62 (noise scale 1.2) so the raking light breaks unevenly across the leaf.

fixes.problem: The rhythm fix landed (gap 75 against pools 168-181 graded), but the pools are now brighter than in round 2 (about 140), and the floor is still by far the brightest large surface. The cool pool from the fitting at 9.4 sits directly in front of the visitation door and outshines it: doorway interior about 122, graded R/B 1.39, tan rather than amber. The warm wedge on the floor shows only as a 10 px tint at the threshold. The eye lands on the floor, not on the destination.
fixes.fix: In FITTINGS, set the 9.4 fitting's level from 1.0 to about 0.5 (or move it to y=8.8), and lower FIT_W from 280 to about 220, so the pools peak at 120-135 graded. In TRIMS['corridor'], raise room_warm from 900 to about 1300 and vd_floor_wedge from 1100 to about 1600, and widen the wedge's cone from 60 to 75 deg so it lies 2-3 m out of the door past the dying tube's footprint. Target: the doorway interior at 150-170 graded, the brightest thing in the lower two thirds, with R about 1.6x B, and a warm wedge at least 60 px deep on the floor before the cool pool takes over.

fixes.problem: The prop's lumpy, melted geometry still shows. On the leaf side of the new barrel knuckle (around x 820-850, y 90-210) a crumpled blob remains from the generated hinge. The generated food hatch is cut by the bottom edge (x 500-750, y 650-720) and reads as warped plates. The same hatches show on every corridor door as pale crumpled shapes (around x 480, 840 and 1150-1280 at y 400-640).
fixes.fix: In door_proto(), cut the prop's own hinge and hatch faces the way the bars are cut: delete the faces inside the hatch box and the hinge zone by local-coordinate bounds. Then build, for every closed door, a clean hatch in hinges()/cell_doors(): a flap box 0.36 x 0.012 x 0.15 m with a 3 mm bevel set in a 20 mm pressed surround, two 18 mm hinge knuckles on its lower edge, and a slide bolt (a 60 x 14 x 10 mm box with an 8 mm knob) at the top, in the door_steel paint. Cover the hinge zone with a flat leaf plate (0.05 x 0.004 x 0.12 m, four 5 mm countersunk heads). For the door camera also tilt the aim about 3 cm higher so the hatch is either fully in frame or clear of the bottom edge.

fixes.problem: Behind the bars, the bottom of the window shows a hard black-and-white triangle pattern (whatever surface the cell_close_night lights hot, cut by the bar and tie-bar shadows), and ghost reflections in the glass fill the upper half. The empty bunk the camera was framed for still does not read.
fixes.fix: In close_cell(), lower cell_close_night from 140 W to about 60 W and move it to the cell's far end wall at z 1.9, aimed back toward the door, so it rims the mattress's near edge and the folded blanket rather than lighting their top faces flat. Add a soft 0.6 x 0.8 m, 15 W cool area grazing the cell's latch-side wall behind the bunk, so the bunk's rail, mattress edge and blanket fold read as a silhouette against a lit wall. Lower the mattress by about 6 cm so the window sees its front edge, not its top. Cut the glass reflections by setting thin_glass refl from 0.05 to about 0.015 for the close door. Check that nothing behind the bars goes above about 170 graded or below about 8.

fixes.problem: The 'worn painted floor' of the beat does not read. At 1280 the floor is a clean, smooth grey lightbox under each pool with no visible scuffs or paint wear. The saw-cut joint at 2.4 m falls exactly on the pool's falloff edge beside the drain, so the pool looks cut off by a ruled line. The drain's stain now reads as a saturated orange decal on one side of the grate.
fixes.fix: In floor_paint (corridor floor), add dark heel and trolley scuffs: a noise stretched about 8:1 along Y, thresholded to about 5% coverage, at 0.6x the paint value, roughness +0.15. Widen roughness variation along the path to 0.38-0.72, so each fitting's reflection breaks into soft streaks instead of an even glow. Raise the contrast between bare and paint slightly (bare about 1.25x paint at path_lift 1.2). Set joint_off so the joint lands about 0.6 m from the pool edge (for example joint_off 0.8). Keep the rust stain to within about 4 cm of the grate, at half its present saturation, and let the damp patch carry the shape.

fixes.problem: The left fifth of the frame is pure black (mean 1.7/255) and the right edge is about 6. The visitor's own chair, which should carry half of the absence, has its seat and back lost in the black; only its tubes read.
fixes.fix: For the chair camera, add to TRIMS a vd_spill of about 35-45 W (the corridor's cool light through the open doorway behind the lens), turned about 20 deg toward -x so it rims the near chair's backrest and seat edge and lifts the left wall's coursing to about 12-20/255. Alternatively raise the near chair's val from 0.4 to about 0.55 and turn it about 10 deg so its backrest catches the pendant spill. Target: the near chair's back reads at 30-45/255 against a wall at 10-15.

fixes.problem: The left 15% of the frame (x 0-180) is a dead black slab (mean 1/255). Beside it, a blank rectangular plate (x 185-275, y 55-200) sits alone on the leaf's edge, unexplained.
fixes.fix: Either reframe 3-4 deg toward the window (aim x shifted so the black jamb strip is under 8% of the frame), or let door_rake's spread (70 to about 95) graze the reveal so the jamb reads at 10-18/255. Remove the stray plate or make it the visible top hinge leaf matching the new knuckle.

fixes.problem: The light under the back door is a uniform hard line peaking at 231/255. It reads as an LED strip rather than daylight-cool light leaking under a door, and its fan on the floor is very short.
fixes.fix: In back_door(), lower the bd_under glow strength from 2.2 to about 1.0. Raise bd_under_light from 3.5 to about 6 W and tip it 20 deg down instead of 12, so the light fans 30-40 cm across the floor tiles with a soft falloff. Target peak about 170 graded.

fixes.problem: On the open hatch the cup, bowl and napkin blow out to near-white blobs against the dark door, so they read as shapes rather than objects. The end wall round the visitation door is mottled noise in the raw frame rather than painted block with mortar lines.
fixes.fix: Lower the tray items' albedo to about 0.4 (cup, bowl, lid) or the hatch slot light by about 30%, so the tray contents peak at about 170 graded with visible shading. Give the end wall the same block_wall material (mortar coursing, dado) as the side walls.

fixes.problem: A faint out-of-focus grey sliver is cut by the right frame edge (x 1265-1280, y 60-220).
fixes.fix: Identify it (probably the back door's frame or the vent) and nudge the aim 1-2 deg, or darken it, so the edge of the frame stays clean. Recheck after the camera change in the priority-1 fix.

evidence_table.verdict:
Round 2 is better than a first pass. The purses frame is close to usable and the overall noir mood is right. As a stage, though, it would still look like CG next to fern's documents. Five problems recur across the frames.

(1) The desk lamp, which carries the whole lighting story, never reads as a lamp. In the overhead it is a huge black disc that the left frame edge cuts, sitting on a white disc. In the push, the shade is a glowing white bowl floating in black, with no visible arm or base. Its outside is lit white although the bulb faces down, which reads as a self-lit object rather than a rim-lit shade.

(2) The "pool" is not a pool. In the overhead the brightest patch is a hard wedge on the case stack at top centre. The open folder, the letter at lower right and the envelope are all lit about equally, even though they sit 40-70 cm apart. That points to fill or a second source rather than one lamp with inverse-square falloff. Meanwhile 53% of the graded overhead is below 8/255, so the right third and the bottom-left are dead black rather than readable wood.

(3) The paper props read as cards and slates, not paper. The sheets are uniform flat white with denoiser smudges (bottom of the right sheet) instead of cockle. The three "glossy prints in three tones" are all the same near-black with white borders: no gloss highlight, no tonal difference, and they read as empty picture frames. The receipt in the overhead is a flat grey rectangle. The mug is only a dark ring from above, and in the laptop shot it is a featureless black cylinder.

(4) The passport is the weakest object in the set. Corner radius is about 8% of its width, the slab has a plastic matte look, and there is no spine, no cover board or turn-in and no visible spring. In the close-up it reads as a phone or tablet lying on a folder, which is exactly the hero beat. That frame is also mid-grey and murky (p1 = 2, no true dark). The "graduated net" just dims everything rather than shaping it.

(5) Surfaces in the push: the foreground planks are big smooth grey slabs with almost no grain, bevel or wear. The prints on the right become thin white outlines floating in black, which reads like wireframe. The lifted corner is ambiguous: a dark wedge, not clearly a curled sheet in focus.

The laptop frame tells its beat (screen glow, passport across passes), but there is a problem with the screen. It is a flat 170/255 grey slab whose spill barely reaches the keys. The bezel is very thin, so it reads more like a lit card than an LCD in a dark room. The case stack is cut by the left edge, and the lamp named in the brief is not visible.

Purses is the strongest frame: good values, warm tote, gold hardware, wood grain, a believable soft pool. Even so, the tote has graded to mustard/olive rather than cognac, and there is a stray arc mark on the table in front of the satchel. The receipt is too wide for a thermal roll; it looks like a half-curled A6 sheet.

Noise is clean, with no fireflies and no clipping (max 197-246 graded), but denoiser smear shows on the large white sheets. No cast is required. The absence is staged acceptably, though nothing in the frames, such as a chair edge or a pushed-back cup, suggests someone just left the table.

Mean is about 5.9. It is not pro level yet. The top-priority fixes are the lamp silhouette and falloff, the passport model and the paper/print materials.

fixes.problem: The lamp reads as a giant black disc cut by the left frame edge, and the pool is a hard wedge on the case stack while distant props are lit equally (fill, not one practical).
fixes.fix: Move the desk-lamp prop about 0.12-0.18 m toward the frame centre so base, arm and shade are all inside frame with at least 4% margin. Tilt the shade head about 25-35 degrees so the opening points at the open folder. Delete or zero any secondary fill/area light over the letter, pen and envelope. Drive the pool only with a spot (spot_size about 70-80 degrees, blend 0.6-0.8, shadow_soft_size 0.02-0.03) parented inside the shade, aimed at the folder centre, so the letter and envelope sit 1.5-2.5 stops darker than the folder. Add a very low bounce (an area light 0.6x0.6 under the table plane, or world strength around 0.002) so the dead-black right third rises to about 10-18/255 and the wood grain is readable rather than crushed.

fixes.problem: The passport reads as a phone or tablet: rounded plastic slab, no spine, no board edge, no visible sprung cover. Flat, murky, mid-grey light.
fixes.fix: Rebuild the passport in Python as three parts. Back board 125x88x0.9 mm. Page block 123x86x3.5 mm in cream (0.80, 0.76, 0.66), with a slight stack ripple from a Wave modifier (amp 0.15 mm), inset 1 mm from the fore edge. Front board 0.9 mm, hinged at the spine with a 3 mm round spine piece, rotated 4-6 degrees (2.5 does not read) so a visible wedge of page block shows. Corner radius 3-4 mm, not about 8 mm. Use a coated-cloth cover material: base (0.03, 0.05, 0.12), roughness 0.55, a fine noise bump (scale 800, strength 0.08) and a 0.4 mm bevel that picks up the key light. Relight with a single warm spot from front-left at about 30 degrees elevation, so the cover has a gradient falloff and the far half of the folder drops 2 stops. Let the frame's darkest 10% reach 3-6/255, not the current lifted greys. Focus on the near cover edge at f/2.0 so the passes behind go soft.

fixes.problem: The lamp is a floating, uniformly glowing white bowl with no arm or base. The lifted corner of sheet_a is an ambiguous dark wedge. The foreground is a smooth grey slab.
fixes.fix: Make the shade exterior a dark enamel (base 0.05, roughness 0.35) so it shows only a rim highlight. Put the emission on a small bulb mesh inside, and add a weak rim light (area 0.1 m, about 3 W) behind and above the lamp to outline the arm and base against black. Add a thin haze volume (density 0.01-0.015) only inside a cone mesh under the shade so the beam reads. Re-curl sheet_a with a Simple Deform bend of 15-25 degrees over the last 6 cm of one corner, set the DOF focus object to that corner, and give the curl's underside a little light (a small warm point at 1 W under the lamp) so it reads as paper, not a black shape. Add a plank bevel (2 mm), a stronger grain bump (0.15) and some roughness variation (0.45-0.7 noise) to the foreground wood. Lower the camera 2-3 cm so the highlighter and a plank seam lead into the frame.

fixes.problem: The three prints all render as near-black slates in white outlines: no gloss, no three tones. The sheets are flat white with denoiser smudges, not cockled paper. The receipt and mug are unreadable from above.
fixes.fix: Give the prints three distinct blank image tones (dark slate 0.08, mid warm grey 0.25, faded sepia 0.35), clearcoat 0.6, clearcoat roughness 0.08, so each catches a lamp specular streak. Add a 0.3 mm thickness and a 1-2 degree twist so the highlights differ. Give the paper sheets a cockle (Displace with a large-scale noise, scale 4, strength 0.6-1.2 mm, on a 40x56 subdivided grid), a fibre bump (scale 1500, strength 0.03) and a base of (0.80, 0.78, 0.72), not near-white. Render with more samples (128+) or turn the denoiser to OIDN with albedo/normal passes to stop the smudge. Turn the receipt so its curl rises toward the lamp, with a 30-40 mm roll diameter so it reads in plan. Give the mug a lighter interior (0.25) with a liquid disc at 0.02, and a rim highlight, so it reads as a mug and not a ring.

fixes.problem: The screen is a flat grey slab with a weak spill. The bezel is too thin to read as an LCD. The mug is a black can. The case stack is cut by the left edge. The turned-down lamp named in the brief is not visible.
fixes.fix: Widen the bezel to 6-8 mm in near-black glossy (base 0.01, roughness 0.15). Give the screen a slight vertical gradient (top 10% brighter) and a cool tint (0.75, 0.82, 1.0) in emission, strength about 2, and add an area light the size of the screen, 3-5 cm in front of it, facing the keys at about 8-12 W so the keycaps and the passport's top edge pick up a cool rim. Frame or move the case stack about 6 cm right so its end sits inside frame with a margin. Show the lamp base and shade at the left, dimmed to about 15% with a warm bulb, so the 'turned down' beat reads. Give the mug a visible rim highlight and handle silhouette.

fixes.problem: The tote grades toward mustard/olive, not cognac. The receipt is the proportions of an A6 sheet, not a thermal slip. A stray arc mark (the mug ring?) on the front plank looks like a glitch.
fixes.fix: Shift the tote's hue toward red (hue -0.03, sat +0.1), or exempt warm leather from the grade's desaturation with a mask, so it reads cognac (around 0.45, 0.22, 0.10 in the raw frame). Rebuild the receipt at 80 mm wide by 220 mm long with a tighter 20-25 mm curl and a slight long-axis bow. Remove or fade the mug-ring decal in this setup (mix factor 0.3) or move it off the hero plank. Add a small specular kicker (spot, 3 W) to catch the satchel clasp and the top edge of the tote.

fixes.problem: No sense of a person having just been at the table, and the black void has no depth cue.
fixes.fix: Add one absence cue per wide frame, for example a chair-back edge catching the lamp spill at the near table edge, or reading glasses folded by the letter. Place a barely-visible far wall at 2.5-3 m with a 0.5-1% lamp spill (values 4-8/255) so the room has depth without breaking the black-room look.

courtroom.verdict: The story reads and the restraint is right. The wide is the strongest frame: a symmetrical aisle, empty benches and one small grey figure in the dock in front of three empty chairs. The wide would almost cut into a fern film as it is. The set still lets it down in several places. (1) The lighting is flat institutional fill, not a lit island. The dock frame's raw 1st percentile is 69 and the bench frame's is 51, so nothing in those frames goes properly dark. The well, the bench and the backdrop all get the same even light. The promised pool of light on Dawn does not exist: the dock is lit no differently from the clerk's desk or the side tables. (2) There is a clear modelling artefact in all three cameras. Where the backdrop frame's verticals meet its header, the top corners show pure black squares (wide at about x485/787, y65; dock at x455, y25; bench at x905, y38). (3) The Tripo gallery benches are rustic church pews. They have blurry, fibrous plank textures and turned feet, which clash with the crisp, modern pale-wood dock and bench. In the wide, their ends are cut by the bottom corners of the frame. (4) The bench camera spends about 70% of the frame on one flat grey wall panel and the bottom 28% on a flat pale fascia slab. The empty chairs are left in a thin band, and the centre-to-wing step reads as a seam, not a lit return. (5) In the dock frame, Dawn's top reads as a casual T-shirt rather than prison clothing. Her one visible hand lies flat on a post knob, not palms-on-the-ledge. The 'f/2.8' background is nearly sharp. The clerk's dead grey monitor slab is the second-strongest shape in the frame and competes with her. (6) There is a stray diamond-shaped object on the upper-left wall between the windows in the wide. The aisle runner stops mid-aisle. The left judge's place has no microphone in the bench view, and no bench microphones read in the wide. The materials are clean and believable at a distance, but they have no wear. The judge chairs show Tripo crumple blotches. Noise and grain are fine, nothing clips, and there are no fireflies. This is competent previs, not yet a finished frame.

fixes.problem: Pure black squares at both top corners of the backdrop frame, where the vertical pilasters meet the header. There is a gap, or open/flipped geometry, showing the void or a backface.
fixes.fix: In the backdrop-frame builder, lengthen the header box by one pilaster width on each side (header x-extent = panel width + 2*pilaster_w) so it overlaps the pilaster tops by the full section. Alternatively, add a corner block box (pilaster_w x pilaster_d x header_h) with the same pale-wood material at each corner. Run bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals on both and make sure neither box has a dark/emission default material. Check from the bench camera at 960x540 --nocast.

fixes.problem: There is no lit island: the well, the bench and the backdrop are evenly filled, and Dawn is not in the 'one pool of light'. The dock and bench frames have no deep shadow (raw p1 69 and 51).
fixes.fix: Cut the general ceiling-panel/fill area lights by about 60% (or delete the largest fill). Add one area light directly over the dock: about 2.8 m up, 1.0x1.0 m, spread about 35 deg, roughly 120-200 W at exposure -1.5, so the dock and Dawn sit about 1.5 stops above the bench fascia. Light the backdrop with a narrow wall-grazer at the cap line (an area light 3 m x 0.1 m, aimed up, about 40 W) so the panel falls off toward the ceiling. Bring in the high windows as cool area lights (4000 K equivalent, about 30 W each), throwing soft shafts through haze density about 0.012 onto the side walls. Target raw p1 below 25 in the dock and bench frames, with the side walls and pews still readable.

fixes.problem: About 70% of the frame is one flat grey panel and about 28% is a flat fascia slab. The chairs sit in a thin band, and the centre-to-wing return does not read.
fixes.fix: Move the camera about 1.2 m further left and 0.4 m lower (eye height 1.45 m), aim it about 30-35 deg off the bench axis, and switch to a 50-65 mm lens so the three chairs fill the middle third. Keep the recessed panel's lower edge just inside the top quarter. Give the wing return its own light: a 0.1 x 0.6 m vertical area light, about 15 W, just off the return face, or angle the cap grazer so the return face is 1 stop brighter than the fascia front. Put a microphone at the left judge's place too, mic base on the desk top 0.25 m to the right of each chair.

fixes.problem: The gallery benches are rustic church pews with blurry, fibrous Tripo textures that clash with the modern pale wood. The near pew ends are cut at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners.
fixes.fix: Build the gallery benches in Python from the same wood() material as the dock: 2.0 m long, 0.45 m seat on 3 slats of 0.12 x 0.03 m, a back of 2 slats up to 0.88 m, 30 mm-thick end panels with a 6 mm bevel and a plain plinth, with no turned feet. Make the near rows about 15% darker in value so they frame the aisle. Then tilt the wide camera up about 1.5 deg, or move the first row back 0.6 m, so no bench end is cut by the bottom corners.

fixes.problem: The f/2.8 look is not there: the chairs and panel are nearly sharp. The clerk's monitor is a dead grey slab that competes with Dawn.
fixes.fix: Set cam.data.dof.use_dof = True, focus_object = Dawn's head bone or empty (focus about 1.7 m), aperture_fstop 2.0, lens 50 mm, so the chairs at about 6 m blur by roughly 8-12 px at 1280. Turn the monitor about 160 deg so only its dark back shows, or remove it. If it stays facing camera, give the screen a faint emission (strength 0.3, cool grey) with a 15 mm bezel at value 0.05. Shift the clerk's desk about 0.3 m right and 0.2 m back so the papers are not a hot spot near the frame's centre of weight.

fixes.problem: Dawn's top reads as a casual T-shirt only slightly darker than the skin, not as prison clothing. In the wide, her shirt is mid-grey, not the 'dark-shirted figure'. Her visible hand lies flat on a post knob, not palms-on-the-ledge.
fixes.fix: Keep dawn_prison() but drop the garment tint to about 0.05-0.06 linear before FABRIC_VALUE, so the shirt is at least 2 stops below the skin in the graded frame. Repose with rigged.pose_figure: chest down about 8 deg, head down about 22 deg, both arms forward about 35 deg with elbows about 25 deg, wrists about 20 cm out from the body's centre, palms on the flat ledge (not the corner post), fingers curled 15 deg. Stand her about 8 cm behind the ledge. Check that both hands show from the dock camera and that neither forearm reads as coming out of her waist.

fixes.problem: There is a stray diamond-shaped object on the upper-left wall between the windows. The aisle runner ends abruptly halfway up the aisle.
fixes.fix: Find and delete the rotated object at about wall height 4 m between the two left windows. If it is meant as a speaker, rebuild it as a flush 0.25 x 0.35 x 0.12 m box aligned to the wall. Extend the runner from the back wall to the bar gates (one continuous strip, 1.0 m wide), or delete it.

fixes.problem: The materials are clean CG. There is no wear on the fascias, dock base or floor. The Tripo judge chairs show crumple blotches. The floor is a flat dark grey.
fixes.fix: Add a 0.1 m dark skirting board (value 0.04, roughness 0.6) along the bench fascia, the dock plinth and the clerk's desk. Add a noise-driven roughness variation (0.45-0.65) and a faint darker kick band in the lowest 0.15 m of the fascias and the dock. Load the judge-chair props with val about 0.4 and rough_add 0.25 to kill the crumple highlights. Give the floor tiles a 3 mm grout groove and a roughness range of 0.35-0.55 so the dock light makes a soft sheen pool on the floor around the dock.

home.verdict: Most round-1 fixes landed. The chair close-up's haze veil, vertical streak and doubled-chair read are gone. The dining wide is no longer crushed (6.7% of pixels at or below 5/255, down from 51%), and the head chair now stands alone on the right third with its striped shadow clear beside it, so both Ch 10 frames now carry the ending. It is still not at fern level. In the kitchen, Dawn's right hand is cocked up off the trackpad with straight, fanned fingers reaching to the lid, which reads as waving at or touching the screen, and the right third is a dead black void. In the dining wide, the hero chair has no tonal separation from the wall behind it (78 vs 76/255), so its shadow and a bright bowl take the eye. The close-up's lower half is murky, and the chair's legs dissolve into the floor with no readable contact.

fixes.problem: Dawn's right hand is tipped up about 28 deg at the wrist and rises roughly 11 cm above her forearm. Its fingers are straight and fanned, and the tips meet the laptop lid's left edge. It reads as waving at or touching the screen, not as the 'finger on the trackpad' the module intends. The brightest pixel in the frame (177/255) is on these fingers, right beside her face. The brief names this failure ('not hovering or splayed'), and round 1's flat mitten hand has become a more visible error.
fixes.fix: In arms_on_table, stop the deck-clearance loop from tipping the hand back. Rest the right wrist on the laptop's palm rest: wrist target z = K_TOP + 0.0175 + 0.022, about 4 cm in from the laptop's front edge. Set hand_pitch to +4 to +6 deg (down) and PITCH_MIN to about -6, so the solver lifts the wrist instead of cocking the hand. Cut the right hand's CURL to knuckle 10-15 and joints 12-18, with the index at 5/8 reaching the trackpad's near half and the thumb tucked along it. A simpler option that is safer from this angle: rest the right hand palm down on the table just left of the laptop, fingers curled 15-20 deg and wrist 2 cm above the top, and give the trackpad to her left hand, which the lid hides. Check from the kitchen camera that no fingertip rises above the lower third of the lid and that a sliver of table shows under the palm.

fixes.problem: The head chair has almost no tonal separation from the unlit wainscot behind it (graded top rail and spindles 77-78/255, wall 76), and the stripes barely mark the chair itself. The eye lands first on its shadow, the highest-contrast shape in the frame, and then on the bowl. The beat asks for the stripes to cross the table and the chair.
fixes.fix: Move HEAD_CHAIR y from 0.02 to about 0.14, or swing the 'street' spot's target y from 0.0 to about +0.12, or both. The chair's right stile and top rail should overlap the patch's lit left (jamb) edge by about 40 px, so the back is silhouetted against the stripes and the slat light crosses its top rail and spindles. Cut the fill on the wall left of the patch for this camera only, TRIMS['dining'] = {'d_sky': 0.6}, and add back d_sky_end if the near table end drops under about 15/255. Graded targets: striped top rail at least 115, unlit wall left of the chair at most 55, shadow still at least 120 px clear of the chair.

fixes.problem: The lower 40% of the frame is a murky mass: the bottom half averages 18/255 and 39% of it sits at or below 12. The seat (16) and the turned legs merge with the oak (18), and the feet's contact cannot be read even with the contact decals. The only floor stripes are a strip at the foot of the wall, away from the chair. The back's crest also catches only faint stripes, so the chair is the dimmest thing in its own close-up.
fixes.fix: Lower and steepen the 'street' spot so its slat stripes land on the boards around and behind the chair's feet: direction d = (0.9, -0.36, -0.34) normalised, target (4.45, 0.0, 0.5) in place of (0.9, -0.36, -0.27) and z 0.66. The legs and their contact shadows then show as dark silhouettes on lit stripes. Graded targets: floor stripes round the feet 45-60, legs at most 20. Re-check the dining wide: the end-wall patch should still start above the chair rail and the shadow should still clear the chair. If the patch drops too far, raise the spot rather than lowering its target. Also raise chair_head's wood value about 15% (tune_prop val) so the stripes across its seat and back read.

fixes.problem: The right third of the frame is a dead black void: graded mean 4/255, and 38% of the whole frame sits at or below 5. The raw has a plain unlit wall there, which the grade's vignette crushes. Nothing on that side tells the room, so the frame weighs left, and the dressing added in round 2 (dish rack, range, fruit bowl) is mostly lost in the dark.
fixes.fix: Give the screen glow something to land on at the right. Option one: a fridge, 0.75 x 0.7 x 1.75 m, satin off-white enamel (albedo about 0.45, roughness 0.35, 0.02 bevel, vertical bar handle), at the right end of the counter run 1.5-2 m behind her, where its door edge and handle catch the laptop's cool spill. Option two: a doorway in the right wall with a dim cool hall light (area 0.4 x 2.0 m, 3-5 W) that leaves a sliver of lit jamb. Target the right third at 12-20 graded with one readable silhouette, still well below her face (about 100-140).

fixes.problem: The white bowl is the brightest object after the stripes (rim 150/255, as bright as the brightest stripe) and sits on the left third, a second subject that pulls the eye away from the head chair. The module's comment says it is 'out of the light', but it is not.
fixes.fix: Darken mt.ceramic('bowl') from 0.4 to about 0.2 and raise its roughness from 0.3 to 0.5, or move d_bowl about 0.3 m toward the far chairs (DT[0] - 0.7, DT[1] + 0.2) into shadow. Target: rim at most 90 graded.

fixes.problem: The dining tabletop reads as rough-sawn barn timber: deep cracks and checks come from the prop's baked normals, and the finish is grey and ashy. It does not read as a family dining table, and the street light leaves no sheen along it.
fixes.fix: In dining_table, cut the prop's baked normal-map strength on the top to about 0.35, or halve the late_k bump, and drop the crack contrast. Add a satin clear coat (coat 0.25, coat roughness 0.25) so the blind stripes leave a soft gleam along the top toward the head chair.

fixes.problem: chair_n2's dark back (12/255) is the largest shape in the frame and is cut by the bottom edge, and its top rail cuts the tabletop in two halfway to the head. The leftmost chair is a half-chair cut by the left edge, and the bright blinds are cut by the top-left edge.
fixes.fix: Push chair_n2 from (2.42, -0.42) to about (2.2, -0.30) so its seat goes under the top and its rail sits lower and further left, or remove it so the top runs unbroken to the head chair. If the cut chair at the left edge still reads as a fragment, nudge the camera loc x by +0.1 or pan about 2 deg right, keeping the head chair on the right third.

fixes.problem: The lidded ceramic jar on the sideboard (d_jar + d_jarLid) reads as a cremation urn in the chapter about Gene Hunt's death, which implies a fact the film has no source for. Its lid also sits about 7 px from the top frame edge, a tangent.
fixes.fix: Remove d_jarLid and turn d_jar into a low open vase about 0.18 m tall, or replace it with a shallow bowl, or leave just the candlesticks. Keep its top under about 1.06 m so it clears the chair camera's top edge by at least 30 px.

fixes.problem: The pale kettle sits directly behind her shoulder and neck, and its lower edge touches her contour (around x 560-600, y 330-340), so it looks like a lump growing out of her shoulder. The paper-towel stand's bright top knob over a pale cylinder reads as a lit pillar candle.
fixes.fix: Slide k_kettle, k_kettleHandle and k_kettleSpout about 0.15 m along the range away from her head, leaving at least 25 px of tile between the kettle and her neck. Make the paper-towel stand's knob dark bronze (value 0.08, roughness 0.5), and make the loose sheet (k_ptSheet) catch more light so the roll reads as paper.

fixes.problem: Inside the stripe patch the wainscot panels read flat. Each stile is a single dark hairline (dining around x 1015 and x 1240, chair close-up along the panels), not a moulding with relief, so the raking street light does not reveal the panelling.
fixes.fix: Model the panel frames 9-12 mm proud of the field with a 4 mm bevel (or a small ogee), so the street light draws a lit edge and a shadow edge along each stile and rail.

fixes.problem: The T-shirt reads as a smooth moulded shell, with no folds at the waist, under the arm or at the sleeve where her right arm crosses forward.
fixes.fix: In cloth() for the shirt, add a low-frequency wrinkle bump (noise scale 5-8, strength 0.12-0.18, distance 0.004) masked toward the waist and the armpits, keeping the fine woven bump, so the shirt reads as cotton.

fixes.problem: The shared grade's vignette in shoot.py (vignette angle PI/4.4) takes the corners to about 30% of raw. It roughly halves the dining stripe patch at the right edge (raw about 140, graded about 71) and crushes the kitchen's right third. This file is not the stage author's to change.
fixes.fix: For the orchestrator: soften the vignette to about PI/5.5, or make it a per-stage setting. Until then, frame the key light motifs (the stripe patch, the hero chair) inside the central 70% of the frame, and judge the corners on the graded frame.

void_stage.verdict: Clearly better than round 1. The suit now covers the body, the bunk is painted steel, cell_close is level and its light falls off upward, cell_far reads at once as the small lit box in the black, and bags is a worthy last image with a gap between the two bags. It is still not pro level because the one human beat fails: Dawn's hands are still splayed claws held away from her thighs, in the dawn camera she looks level at the lens with a faint grin instead of bowing her head, and her prison greys read as a skin-tight T-shirt and leggings with no folds; around her the pool is still a flat disc under a column of haze that does not taper, and the cell is a clean clay render whose window shaft seems to land on the back wall instead of reaching its patch on the floor.

fixes.problem: Round-1 hand fix did not land. Both hands are still open claws: the fingers are fanned apart and curled forward, the palms face forward and in, and the hands hang 5-8 cm off the trouser seam, as if she is about to grab something. POSE['fingers'] = 16 only curls the fingers. The spread comes from the MakeHuman rest pose and nothing closes it.
fixes.fix: After rigged.pose_figure and straight_wrists, close and curl each finger bone on both sides directly. Curl (local X) proximal/middle/distal: index 10/15/10, middle 14/20/12, ring 17/24/15, pinky 20/27/17 degrees, so the curl grows from index to pinky. Adduct (local Z) toward the middle finger: index 4, ring 4, pinky 8 degrees, until the gaps between fingers are under 3 mm. Bring thumb.01 about 20 degrees toward the palm so it lies along the side of the index. Lower the arm 'out' value in POSE['l_arm'] and POSE['r_arm'] from 7/6 to 2-3, and pronate the forearms about 20 degrees so the palms face the outer thighs, 2-4 cm off the trouser side seam. Check both hands at 100 % with VOID_DEBUG=1 (dbg_dawn and dbg_dawn_high).

fixes.problem: In the camera that carries Ch 07 the head does not read as bowed. From 1.2 m, a head down of 18 degrees on a 1.6 m figure is about level with the lens, so she looks straight at us. The lower lip catches light, which reads as a faint grin. The top-lit sculpted hair is the brightest thing in frame (raw about 0.78, brighter than the 0.46 pool), so it reads as a white swim cap over a black face. Defeat reads as calm or even pleasant.
fixes.fix: POSE['head'] (18, 3) -> (28, 3) and POSE['neck'] (4, 0) -> (7, 0). Keep chest at 2.5 so dawn_high does not stoop again. The mouth then falls into the shadow of the brow and nose. If the MakeHuman base has an expression or mouth shape key, set it to neutral with the mouth closed. In light_suit, give the hair its own netted copy of the lamp at 0.35 instead of 0.55, or set the hair albedo to about 0.33, so the crown lands near 0.6 raw. The crown stays the brightest point on her without reading as a helmet.

fixes.problem: The covering fix landed, but the outfit reads as athleisure, not prison issue. It is a fitted T-shirt and leggings that hug the bust, hips, thighs and calves, with no folds anywhere. The creases Displace (strength 0.006, cloud scale 0.045) is invisible at this distance, and the trousers taper to the ankle like tights.
fixes.fix: Loosen the garment and give it drape, in this stage only. (a) Raise the 'standoff' Displace push from 0.005 to 0.012. Add a vertex group 'leg_fall' on the trousers, weight 0 at the knee to 1 at the hem, with a second Displace of 0.025 on it, so the legs fall straight from the knee instead of wrapping the calf. Raise the shirt hem 2 cm off the hips the same way, so it hangs untucked like a tunic. (b) Better: run a short cloth sim on the inflated garment. Pin a group of collar, shoulder seams and waistband. Make the body a Collision with 3 mm outer thickness. Quality 5, mass 0.15 kg, 30 frames, then apply. That gives real folds at the waist, the inner elbows, behind the knees and 2-3 rings stacked above the shoes. (c) If you keep the Displace route, raise creases to strength 0.014, noise_scale 0.08 and stretch 3.5, so 3-6 horizontal folds read at waist, knees and ankles. If people.dawn_prison() cannot give a looser two-piece, say so in the report so the cast owner can.

fixes.problem: Pale stone shows at the heel and toe of the frame-right shoe in both frames, so it looks like an open sandal or a foot through the shoe. There is also a small white speck at the frame-left temple, just under the hairline (the ear or a gap at the hair edge catching the top light).
fixes.fix: In suit_fit, run the same covered test against the shoe meshes (Dawn's children whose names contain 'shoes'). Use it for the DEF-foot and DEF-toe vertices, which KEEP currently exempts, and tuck the covered ones 8 mm. A closed shoe can also take a Mask (invert) on those vertices, because no gap shows inside it. For the temple, extend the hair cap 5 mm down over the top of the ear, or put the ear vertices in the 'handmask'-style darker stone (0.35) at specular 0.15. Recheck in dbg_dawn.

fixes.problem: The beam still does not taper. In dawn the haze is a vertical column about 1.8 m wide, the same at frame top and at her shoulders (graded 13-21 across the same x range at y 100 and y 300). In dawn_high it is a grey slab whose sharp vertical edges run straight up. The round-1 advice to raise the lamp to 9-10 m was physically wrong: a higher lamp with the same pool makes the cone more parallel (half-angle atan(1.2/9.5) = 7 degrees), so the 3 m of beam in frame cannot taper.
fixes.fix: SPOTS['dawn']: h 9.5 -> 5.2, watts 18500 -> about 5600 (inverse square, (5.2/9.5)^2), fwd -0.5 -> -0.3, pool 1.2 and blend 0.28 kept. The half-angle becomes about 13 degrees, so in dawn the lit beam narrows from 2.4 m at the floor to about 1.1 m at the frame top: a cone coming down out of the dark, not a curtain. In _spot_and_haze pass r_top 0.05 instead of 0.35 so the haze frustum follows the cone to its point. Confirm the lamp stays out of dawn_high's frame (it sits about 34 degrees off that camera's axis).

fixes.problem: The pool is still a flat disc. In dawn the raw floor runs 114 at the edge to about 130 at the centre, about 14 % in display values, and then cuts off over about 30 px. Inside the pool in the dawn frame only one board seam shows, so the floor reads as a CG disc. Bags is better (graded 92 -> 132) but still evenly flat on its front half.
fixes.fix: For the dawn and bags spots, call st.hotspot(main, frac=0.5, gain=0.9) instead of (0.62, 0.35), so the centre is about 1.9x the edge in linear light. Widen the main spot blend from 0.28 to 0.34 so the edge rolls off over about 15 cm. On the hardboard, raise per-board value variation to plus or minus 5 %, and add very low-contrast scuffs and old tape marks (thin dark streaks, 0.9x value, roughness 0.75), so the lit centre shows a worked stage floor.

fixes.problem: The window shaft and its patch do not connect. The shaft travels almost straight toward the lens, so it is foreshortened into a vertical curtain down the back wall. Its lower part sits over a floor that is nearly as bright as it is (raw floor about 170-180), so it vanishes, and the shaft seems to end at the base of the wall about 1.3 m behind the patch. The patch is weak: graded 172 against 144 for the floor around it, about 1.2:1, and the window glass (96) is darker than the floor.
fixes.fix: Make the window the lead after the floor. (a) Darken the back half of the cell floor under the top spot. Move SPOTS['cell'] fwd 0.0 -> +0.35 (the pool's hot centre toward the open side) and cut watts 13500 -> 11000, so the floor between the back wall and the patch lands near 0.35 raw. (b) Raise WINDOW_W by 1.5x (to about 260000) so the patch is near 0.8 raw, a 2:1 patch-to-floor ratio, and the shaft then reads over the darker floor all the way down to the patch. (c) Rake the night source about 15 degrees about Z toward +X (move it sideways behind the slot rather than straight back), so the patch shifts about 0.35 m to frame left and the shaft runs on a visible diagonal instead of straight at the lens. Rebuild haze_box_along on the new ray. Keep SHAFT_HAZE at 0.08.

fixes.problem: The cell is a clean clay render. Every surface is one value and one roughness. There is no grime at the wall bases, no wear on the bunk paint, the desk and stool are crisp grey primitives, and the books are plain slabs with no page block. Under the upper deck the lower bunk is a black hole: the 0.04-0.066 vinyl mattress disappears. The lower blanket is the lightest cloth in frame and hangs like stiff paper, with a wavy cut edge.
fixes.fix: Wall paint: darken 15-20 % within 15 cm of the floor (an AO or height mask), and add a faint water stain 30-40 cm down from the window splay. Bunk paint: edge wear from Pointiness or AO showing darker steel at the post feet, the ladder rung and the rail tops (value 0.6x, roughness 0.35, mask coverage about 8 %). Desk: chip its front edge and add a slightly lighter, smoother rub patch where forearms rest. Books: confirm the 'book pages' material is on an inset page block 3 mm inside the covers, with page lines (a wave texture at scale 400 across the thickness). Mattress vinyl: rgb (0.04, 0.05, 0.066) -> about (0.10, 0.11, 0.12), so the lower mattress's top edge and front lip read. Blanket: wool value 0.085 -> 0.06, and drop 0.2 -> 0.12, with 3-4 vertical folds (noise stretched 1:6 down the drop) and a straight hem instead of a wavy cut.

fixes.problem: The bags read as two dark lumps against a dark grey haze backdrop. Their tops are only 0.21-0.38 raw, their sides 0.03-0.12, and the haze behind them about 0.1, so the silhouettes barely separate. They sit in the back half of the pool, with a band of empty lit floor in front, and they fill only about a third of the frame height for the film's last image.
fixes.fix: Move the bags spot's aim to the bags' centroid (G + (0.0, -0.04)) so they stand at the pool's centre and hotspot. Push in: camera y -4.7 -> -4.0, or lens 50 -> 60, so the case is about 42-45 % of frame height with the whole pool edge still in frame. Add an invisible back rim linked to the two bags only: an area light 0.6 x 0.6 m, about 40 W, at (G.x, G.y + 2.4, 1.5) aimed at the bags. The case's telescoping handle, its top edge, and the duffel's straps and top seam then catch a fine 0.45-0.55 line against the haze, while the faces stay dark.

fixes.problem: Framing: the frame bottom cuts the stool's pedestal and base, and its pale top (graded 129) is a flat disc in the foreground that competes with the patch.
fixes.fix: Tuck the stool under the desk (move it about 0.35 m toward the left wall and 0.15 m back), so it is fully in frame and half in the desk's shadow. Or move it out of shot. Darken its seat to the bunk paint value (about 0.27) with roughness 0.55.

fixes.problem: Ch 08 is 'what twelve years can take', but nothing in the cell marks time. The dressing (towel, books, folded bedding) is what a newly issued cell would hold.
fixes.fix: Add two restrained signs of long occupancy, dark and low in contrast, with no text. One: a small bundle of plain envelopes tied with a band on the desk beside the books (letters from home, about 5 envelopes at 0.11 x 0.22 m, warm off-white at value 0.45 so the grade keeps them quiet). Two: a plastic cup and a toothbrush on the steel unit's ledge, the cup() helper at r 0.036. Optionally a few faint tally-like scratches low on the wall beside the lower bunk, as a bump only with no value change, so they never read as text or numbers.

fixes.problem: Small leftovers. A faint sliver of spill (raw 17-44) lies on the void floor just under the slab's front edge. The beam's haze stops dead at the plane of the wall tops, so the cone reads as ending above the box instead of falling into it.
fixes.fix: Pull the cell pool's front edge in 5 cm (ry 2.05 -> 2.0, or after the fwd change in the window fix, check that the spill line is gone). Extend the top spot's haze down into the box at a lower density (0.004) so the cone visibly continues past the wall tops onto the floor.

hearing_room.verdict: Most round-1 fixes landed. HANDS now sits in the stage's exposure (graded mean 30, sleeve 40 against hand 132, paper peak 157) with a clean left-over-right fold and a stacked paper pile. The WIDE's crush fell from 49% to 17% of pixels at or below 3/255: sconces, housed broadcast lights and a clerk's table now tell the room. DAIS is a real low angle and its fascia falls off (13 graded under chairs at 64). It is still not at fern level, and most of what holds it back is in the WITNESS medium. Tim still reads as a smooth, androgynous man of about 30 whose hair is a shell with a raised step at the hairline. His face is lit almost flat (about 1.15:1). The shirt tone leaks onto the tie in pale flecks. The microphone stands at his shoulder while he looks away from it. The rows behind him crush to black (1.6 graded on the right), so 'empty rows behind' does not read. In the WIDE, the evenly washed blue drape (mean 71) pulls the eye harder than Tim's pool of light, its pleat tops end in a picket-fence row of pointed tips, and the lower-tier desk cap runs through the top of his head.

fixes.problem: Tim does not read as a man in his mid-fifties, even at TIM_AGE 0.78 and weight 0.7. The face is smooth with a small jaw. The chin is raised 18 degrees, which shows a long thin neck standing inside a loose collar ring. The receded hair is a smooth shell that ends in a visible raised step all round the hairline (temples and front), so it reads as a swim cap or wig edge. The face is lit almost flat: lit half 137 against shadow half 120 graded (about 1.15:1), which wipes out the form that would carry age on a stone statue.
fixes.fix: (a) TIM_UPPER head (-18, -16) -> about (-8, -8). Less chin-up shortens the neck in view, fills the collar and turns the face toward the mic and the dais. (b) Widen the neck about 12% and the jaw about 8%. Use MakeHuman targets if cast.person exposes them (neck-scale-horiz-incr about 0.35, chin-width-incr about 0.3, head-square about 0.3). Otherwise bind a 2x2x3 Lattice to the neck and jaw vertex groups. Pull the shirt collar ring about 6 mm in so it sits on the neck. (c) In recede_hair, ramp the 'volume' weights from 0 at the new edge to 1 over 25 mm, and mask soften_hair's clumps displacement to 0 within 15 mm of the edge. At a 5x crop the hair must meet the scalp flush, with no ledge. (d) In TRIMS['witness'], cut tv_fill_light 0.18 -> about 0.06 and leave the key, so the face's lit side is about 140 graded and the shadow side 65-80 (about 2:1), with readable shadow under the brow, cheekbone and jaw.

fixes.problem: Pale, ragged flecks run along the tie's left edge and knot (graded about 90-150 on a tie of 39). The shirt tone leaks onto the tie through holes in suit_tones' tie mask, or the shirt mesh pokes through. It sits on the hero's chest in the controlled medium.
fixes.fix: In suit_tones(), close tie_m before building shirt_m: dilate it by about 6 px (a 13x13 max filter, or scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation iterations=6) and fill holes inside the tie's bounding box. Then remove a 3 px band around tie_m from shirt_m. If flecks remain at a 5x crop of the knot, the cause is geometry: push the tie region out 2-3 mm with a Displace modifier along the normals, restricted to a tie vertex group built from the same mask.

fixes.problem: The drape is the biggest bright mass in the WIDE (mean 71 graded, against 40 for Tim's back and 44 for the table top), so the eye lands on it before the 'one pool of light'. The pelmet's shadow edge on the perfectly regular sine pleats (lam 0.21, one amplitude) cuts the top of every crest into a pointed tip. The result is a picket-fence or icicle fringe along the drape's top in both frames, and the pleats read as a CG comb.
fixes.fix: Add TRIMS['wide'] = {'washer': 0.55} and TRIMS['dais'] = {'washer': 0.75}. In drape(), move the washer slot and source from yb - 0.55 to about yb - 1.1, aim it at (0, yb + 0.1, 2.2) and widen the spread to about 100. The pelmet shadow then sits at the very top and the valleys fill. Alternatively, hide a cove strip under pelmet_lip, aimed straight down. Give each pleat its own pitch (lam x random 0.88-1.12) and amplitude (x 0.8-1.2) from a seeded sequence, so no two folds match. Targets: drape mean in the WIDE 40-48 graded, Tim's crown still the brightest point (at least 180), no pointed crest tips at a 3x crop.

fixes.problem: The lower-tier desk cap runs through the top of Tim's head, a tangency right at the figure the frame is about. The lit crown (208) merges into the lit cap line instead of standing against dark.
fixes.fix: Raise the wide camera from z 2.05 to about 2.4 and the aim z from 1.5 to about 1.6 to keep the framing. The near figure then drops faster than the far dais and his crown lands on the dark fascia panel (about 28 graded). Check that at least 15 px separate the crown from the cap line at 1280.

fixes.problem: He still does not speak into the microphone. The gooseneck head sits at chest height off his left shoulder (screen x about 735, y about 290, with his mouth at about 575, 230), and his head is turned the other way, toward the camera side.
fixes.fix: Re-place mic_tim with mic_place((TIM_X - 0.12, EDGE + 0.30), (TIM_X - 0.02, EDGE - 0.10), 1.15).
